findings.evidence: got-scraping 4.2.1, dist/index.js lines 543-552 and 577-585 (a dependency); packages/engine/src/crawler.ts:575
findings.what: got-scraping's header generator opens a TLS connection (ALPN probe) to each new https host:port with system DNS, ignoring the pinned dnsLookup. With a rebinding hostname (needs only a DNS server the attacker runs) the probe handshakes with an internal ip:port; reproduced: a 1,604-byte ClientHello reached 127.0.0.1, and with useHeaderGenerator:false nothing arrived. No HTTP request is sent on the probe and no body is read, but a failed probe fails the request and the page is stored with status 0, so one audit of https://rebind.example:PORT/ URLs (no port check; same-host strategy matches the hostname only) reads one bit per URL: a blind internal TLS port scan. The request itself still goes over the pinned connection. The port-scan oracle is read from the code, not reproduced; CC-SEC-2 confirms it when fixing.
findings.owner: CC-SEC-2 (engine; crawl-path change needs the deployed-function smoke)

findings.what: /privacy calls rate-limit records short-lived; production holds 1,138 rows, 1,027 older than 30 days, oldest 157 days, 468 keys embedding a raw IP and 52 a raw email; nothing deletes the table (measured 2026-11-09). Fixed by a daily prune of rows past their window (the migration adds public.prune_rate_limits; the cleanup cron calls it). Hashing the keys is a follow-up.

/privacy and /terms promise erasure on request; no code deletes public.users, public.users has no FK to auth.users, and the email also sits unlinked in rate_limits keys, email_events, audits.notify_email, waitlist and takedown_requests. Erasure is possible by hand in SQL; what is missing is the process and the cascade. Fixed by the users_id_auth_fkey cascade, scripts/ops/erase-account.ts and docs/ops/erasure.md.
the id is not validated and the stream has no rate limit: a garbage id polls the database every 2.5 s until the 250 s self-close; its no-cache header lacks private.
owner-only bodies with no Cache-Control; dynamic, not CDN-cached, so hardening.
the engine's validation message is returned verbatim, including the private address a name resolved to.
email has no maximum length.

the per-domain bucket (3 a day) is spent before the report lookup, so three junk posts block a domain's takedown form for a day; Turnstile runs only when a token is sent. No mail is sent. Rated minor because the takedown address (email) remains open when the form is blocked.
a Stripe API call per request with no per-user rate limit (signed-in only).

the middleware sends X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive on every /r/ page, including the claimed, indexable reports the page marks index and the sitemap lists, so no report can be indexed (since 0478f107, before SPEC 04 made claimed reports indexable). A missing report's HTML also carries two robots metas. Changing the header changes what search engines index (§13). Fixed: the header is gone from /r/ and stays on /embed/. The missing report's two robots metas (Next's noindex for the 404 and the root layout's) are unchanged; the 404 status and the noindex keep it out of the index.
"We do not store passwords" while 11 of 12 auth.users rows hold a hash (most likely GoTrue's random password for magic-link sign-ups; not checked against GoTrue source).
email delivery events are not named on /privacy and are never cleaned up (109 rows, 91 older than 30 days, 33 to non-account addresses).
public reports outlive their audits and are never deleted (78 of 96 have a null audit_id); /privacy is silent and Terms §18 says reports are deleted after termination, with no code path.
the crawlmouse_anon cookie (httpOnly, one year) is missing from the cookie list.
email addresses of people without an account (waitlist, takedown requests, audits.notify_email) are not listed.
INNGEST_AUDIT_CONCURRENCY from 6 to 100 passed the old clamp of 100; above the Free cap the whole app sync is rejected. CC-20b clamps it to PLAN_CONCURRENCY_CAP = 5 (inngest/concurrency.ts:13).

the TTL cleanup does not exempt an audit behind a minted report; the report keeps its snapshot (FK on delete set null). One 2026-06-14 report has neither snapshot nor audit and renders through the legacy fallback (apps/web/app/r/[slug]/page.tsx:68).
with INNGEST_DEV set in production the SDK accepts unsigned invocations; nothing in the repo sets it, production env could not be read.
findings.owner: owner: confirm INNGEST_DEV is absent with vercel env ls production

findings.what: the Crawlee path passes extraHeaders without safeFetch's forbidden-header filter; no web route sets it today.
JSON-LD was serialised with bare JSON.stringify into a script tag; every caller passes our own constants today, so this was hardening.

login CSRF with data capture: an attacker requests a magic link for their own address and gets a victim to open it and press Continue; the victim is signed in as the attacker and the victim browser's anonymous audits move into the attacker's account. The foreign-link refusal needed the cm_auth_for cookie, which only the v2 door set, so on v1 it never fired. Disclosed for v2 in docs/specs/v2/25-account-door.md. Fixed: every magic-link request sets cm_auth_for, and the claim needs it to match the signed-in address (§5 change signed off by the owner).

the per-IP throttle runs after the secret check, so wrong-secret guesses are not throttled; it matters only if ADMIN_SECRET is short. The code comment above it (app/api/admin/takedown/process/route.ts:35) says the throttle caps a brute force; the follow-up corrects it too.
